scope: All supplied CSV files; no raw signals or provenance authentication available

checks.note: Inferred from prompt_id date minus study_day; not an original laboratory timestamp.

checks.check: EEG aperiodic mean with stated QC

checks.note: Exact repetition may reflect a shared stage aggregate; raw ECG-derived respiration and algorithm are needed to assess.

findings.title: D31 questionnaire coverage differs from laboratory follow-up
findings.detail: Questionnaire D31 records exist for 230 people, versus 217 laboratory retests and 217 counselor re-evaluations. This may be remote follow-up but is undocumented.

findings.title: Withdrawn participants retained when thresholds met
findings.detail: 4 analyzable participants have withdrew_during_tracking status. This can be defensible if retained-data consent permits and inclusion is based on available data, but needs explicit reporting.

findings.title: EDA calibration extreme ratios
findings.detail: cal_scl_palm_equiv_rel range -1809.254527 to 405.160400; 10/401 have absolute value >100. These are transformed/calibrated units, not physical SCL; inspect small-denominator guards and report sensitivity.

findings.title: Repeated stage respiration values
findings.detail: All 675/675 sessions have identical respiration rate across three stress blocks; this needs a documented aggregation rule, not an assumption of fabricated data.

limitations: No raw ECG/EDA/EEG/PPG/accelerometry or five-minute window tensor supplied, so signal processing and quality flags cannot be independently re-executed.
No actual OSF URL, preregistration, weights or original scripts; timestamp row is a self-reported record, not independent verification.
Some named wrist features require unavailable window-level data, so consistency of person-level tabulations is not equivalent to authenticating measurements.
Validity-day definition includes sleep worn; no separate sleep-worn flag is supplied. Wear>=16h with valid_day=0 is not by itself an error.
Physiological ranges used here are broad audit screens, not clinical or device-specific reference intervals.
Quantitative errors and unusual patterns cannot establish whether a dataset is simulated or fabricated.
